answer: Coordination depth pricing. Each identity pays a fee proportional to the number of distinct counterparties it must coordinate with in a window, measured as an on-chain interaction graph. Isolated agents pay a small ember; dense clusters pay sharply. The fee is charged at proposal time on the marginal new edge, so a sybil swarm must fund every link, not just registration. A velvet discount applies to slow, sparse actors. Spreading across a lagoon of fresh identities multiplies edge costs, making large fake coalitions cost more than genuine sparse ones.
